title: Mock 5 · Distributor Ready
blurb: Investor suitability, reporting, exits and good practices, mixed review.

questions.q: Units of REITs and InvITs are classified in the workbook's comparative listing as which type of investment?
options: Dual (illiquid underlying assets but liquid listed instruments)
questions.explanation: The dual class includes structures with illiquid underlying assets whose instruments are liquid, such as REIT and InvIT units.
hints: Wrong: underlying assets are illiquid real estate/infra.
Wrong: listing gives them liquidity.
Wrong: they are investment instruments.
Correct: illiquid underlying, but units are listed and tradable.

questions.q: As on March 01, 2026, approximately how many AIFs were registered with SEBI?
questions.explanation: As on March 01, 2026, 1802 AIFs were registered with SEBI, starting from just 21 funds in 2012.
hints: Correct: 1802 AIFs as on March 01, 2026.
Wrong: 21 was the count in 2012.
Wrong: not the figure.
Wrong: not the figure.

questions.q: Who is responsible for safekeeping of the securities of an AIF?
options: A SEBI-registered custodian appointed by the sponsor or manager
questions.explanation: Sponsor or Manager of AIFs shall compulsorily appoint a custodian registered with SEBI for safekeeping of securities of the fund.
hints: Wrong: distributors do not hold assets.
Correct: appointing a custodian is compulsory.
Wrong: conflict of interest.
Wrong: investors do not hold fund assets.

questions.q: Under the high watermark concept, if a fund starts the year at ₹100 crore with a 20% hurdle and ends at ₹135 crore, on how much will additional return be computed for the year?
questions.explanation: Up to ₹120 crore (100 + 20%) no additional return is earned; additional return is calculated on the excess, i.e. 135 − 120 = ₹15 crore.
hints: Wrong: ignores the hurdle.
Correct: 135 − 120 = ₹15 crore above the hurdle-adjusted mark.
Wrong: that is the hurdle amount itself.
Wrong: the entire fund value is not the base.

questions.q: A Category I/II AIF wants to invest in units of another AIF managed by an associate of its own sponsor. What approval is needed?
options: Approval of two-thirds of investors by number
Approval of 75% of investors by value of their investment
questions.explanation: AIF shall not invest in associates or units of AIFs managed/sponsored by its manager, sponsor or their associates except with approval of 75% of investors by value.
hints: Wrong: two-thirds by value is for strategy change/extension.
Wrong: investor approval is mandatory.
Correct: 75% by value.
Wrong: this is a restricted related-party investment.

questions.q: AIFs may invest overseas only in equity and equity-linked instruments of offshore venture capital undertakings, subject to a limit of what percentage of the scheme's investable funds?
questions.explanation: Overseas investments shall not exceed 25% of the investable funds of the scheme, within an industry-wide limit of USD 1,500 million.
hints: Wrong: not the overseas limit.
Correct: not more than 25% of investable funds.
Wrong: not the overseas limit.
Wrong: not the overseas limit.

questions.q: In a parallel AIF structure, the offshore fund and the domestic AIF:
options: Merge into a single SEBI-registered pool
Are both registered under SEBI (AIF) Regulations
Are two separate pools with separate management that invest side by side
questions.explanation: In a parallel structure the offshore fund and domestic AIF are kept distinct with separate management structures; it carries several tax and compliance risks.
hints: Wrong: that describes aggregation in the unified structure.
Wrong: the offshore fund follows FVCI/FDI rules.
Wrong: not a feature of the structure.
Correct: the pools are kept distinct with separate managements.

questions.q: Which investor-routing consideration is NOT among the general principles for choosing an offshore pooling jurisdiction?
options: Availability of the highest local corporate tax rate
questions.explanation: Principles include a good DTAA, BIPA, recognised capital market, political/legal/currency stability, and FATF-equivalent jurisdiction.
hints: Wrong: DTAA is of primary importance.
Wrong: FATF compliance is a necessity.
Correct: investors seek tax optimisation, not high taxes.
Wrong: stability matters for wealth preservation.

questions.q: An investor puts in ₹10,000 and gets back ₹19,000 after 3 years. The simple average annual return is 30%. Why is the IRR lower (about 24%)?
options: IRR accounts for the timing of cash flows (time value of money)
questions.explanation: The average approach ignores timing; IRR finds the discount rate equating future cash flows to the investment, giving about 24% in Illustration 6.1.
hints: Wrong: IRR is pre-tax unless specified.
Correct: IRR discounts cash flows over time.
Wrong: the payout is central to IRR.
Wrong: not part of the calculation.

questions.q: Institutional investors often keep forecasted capital calls above their current cash balances to avoid idle cash. This is known as:
questions.explanation: Institutional investors often pursue an over-commitment strategy in which forecasted capital calls on outstanding commitments exceed current cash balances.
hints: Correct: over-commitment strategy.
Wrong: clawback recovers excess carry.
Wrong: catch-up relates to carry distribution.
Wrong: giveback is a waterfall adjustment.

questions.q: Under SEBI's stewardship code, how many principles must institutional investors such as AIFs follow?
questions.explanation: SEBI's stewardship code lays down Principles 1 to 6, ending with periodic reporting on stewardship activities.
hints: Wrong: too few.
Correct: six principles (policy, conflicts, monitoring, intervention, voting, reporting).
Wrong: too many.
Wrong: too many.

questions.q: External members of an Investment Committee whose names were NOT disclosed in the PPM at the time of onboarding can be appointed only with consent of:
options: At least two-thirds of investors by number
At least 75% of investors by value of investment
questions.explanation: Undisclosed external IC members shall be appointed only with consent of at least 75% of investors by value (not needed for ex-officio changes).
hints: Wrong: wrong threshold and basis.
Wrong: investor consent is needed.
Wrong: SEBI does not approve IC members.
Correct: 75% by value.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed in the workbook as an area where alignment of interest between investors and the manager is required?
options: Number of employees in the distributor's firm
questions.explanation: Alignment areas: sponsor commitment, fees and carry, waterfall, catch-up and clawback, outside interests, governance and reporting, related-party transactions and co-investment.
hints: Correct: catch-up and clawback are listed alignment areas.
Wrong: not an alignment area.
Wrong: not an alignment area.
Wrong: not an alignment area.

questions.q: A fund manager sits on the board of a distressed portfolio company and holds information under an NDA that the AIF's duties may require disclosing. This is an example of:
options: Competing or outside interests creating conflict
questions.explanation: Conflict due to outside interests may arise when board positions held by the manager in investee companies compromise the AIF's interests, including NDA disclosure issues.
hints: Wrong: this is a misalignment risk.
Wrong: unrelated.
Wrong: no key person is unavailable.
Correct: board positions can compromise AIF interests and create disclosure dilemmas.

questions.q: A fund that has completed at least how long from first close must report data to benchmarking agencies?
questions.explanation: AIFs/Schemes that have completed at least one year from first close shall provide necessary data to the benchmarking agencies.
hints: Wrong: not the threshold.
Wrong: not the threshold.
Wrong: the trigger is one year from first close.
Correct: at least one year from first close.

questions.q: A European institutional consortium wants long-term exposure to clean-energy technology ventures. Which AIF would a distributor match it with?
options: An AIF investing in equities and green bonds of clean-energy and sustainability technology companies
An AIF focused on oil and gas exploration assets
A digital graphics and 3D printing VC fund
A short-term trading fund in currency derivatives
questions.explanation: In Case 8.2 the European consortium targeting clean-energy assets and technologies is the best fit for the green-tech AIF.
hints: Correct: closely aligned with the investor's objective (Case 8.2).
Wrong: hydrocarbons conflict with clean-energy focus.
Wrong: different sector theme.
Wrong: short-term, leveraged, Category III style.

questions.q: Side letters are executed between:
options: The specific investor, the AIF and the investment manager
questions.explanation: Side letters are executed by the specific investor, the AIF and the investment manager and are not disclosed to other investors.
hints: Wrong: side letters are not common to all investors.
Correct: bilateral to a specific investor with the AIF and manager.
Wrong: unrelated parties.
Wrong: unrelated parties.

questions.q: AI-only funds and Large Value Funds can launch new schemes:
options: Immediately upon filing their PPM with SEBI
Only after SEBI approves the PPM
Only after a merchant banker's due diligence certificate
questions.explanation: AI-only Funds and LVFs are exempt from filing through merchant bankers and can launch schemes immediately upon filing PPM (first scheme from registration date).
hints: Correct: they follow an 'intimation to SEBI' model.
Wrong: no waiting period.
Wrong: SEBI never approves PPMs.
Wrong: they are exempt from filing via merchant bankers.

questions.q: When a close-ended AIF undergoes a material change, dissenting unit holders must be given at least how long to express dissent?
questions.explanation: Unit holders shall be provided not less than one month for expressing their dissent; exit must be completed within 3 months of the last date of the dissent offer.
hints: Wrong: too short.
Wrong: 3 months is the completion window for the exit.
Correct: not less than one month.
Wrong: not prescribed.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'material change' that triggers the exit option for investors?
options: Change in control of the sponsor or manager
Internal restructuring within the manager's group
Change in valuation methodology within prescribed guidelines
Appointment of a new auditor of an investee company
questions.explanation: Material changes include change in sponsor/manager (excluding internal group restructuring), change in control, and fee/hurdle changes leading to higher fees.
hints: Correct: change in control is a material change.
Wrong: internal group restructuring is excluded.
Wrong: explicitly not a material change (disclose both values).
Wrong: not a fund-level material change.

questions.q: Sale of an existing investor's units in an AIF to another investor at an agreed value is called:
questions.explanation: Secondary exit of investor interest, i.e. sale of unit capital to co-investors or outside investors, is known as 'secondaries' and often happens at a substantial discount to NAV.
hints: Wrong: drawdown is a capital call.
Wrong: first close is a fundraising milestone.
Correct: secondaries, usually at a discount to NAV.
Wrong: in-specie means distributing assets instead of cash.

questions.q: According to IPEV Guidelines, the best measure for valuing private equity portfolio companies is:
questions.explanation: The central theme of the IPEV recommendations is that fair value is the best measure for valuing PE portfolio companies and funds.
hints: Wrong: cost is only a starting point.
Wrong: not used for equity.
Correct: fair value is the central theme of IPEV.
Wrong: used only in distress.

questions.q: Non-business losses of a Category I/II AIF are passed through to investors only if the units have been held for at least:
questions.explanation: Losses other than business losses pass through to unit holders if units were held for at least 12 months; they can be carried forward for 8 years.
hints: Correct: at least 12 months.
Wrong: not the threshold.
Wrong: not the threshold.
Wrong: not the threshold.

questions.q: GST in the AIF context is levied on:
options: Investment management fees and trusteeship fees
questions.explanation: GST at the applicable rate is levied on investment management fees and trusteeship fees payable by the AIF.
hints: Wrong: GST is not levied on capital gains.
Wrong: dividends are not services.
Correct: services of the manager and trustee attract GST.
Wrong: commitments are capital, not a service.

questions.q: Which of the following is a POST-commitment service of an AIF distributor?
options: Facilitating fund due diligence before commitment
Coordinating drawdown notices and transfer of funds
questions.explanation: Post-commitment services include liaison on drawdown notices and fund transfers, reporting support, investor requirements and marketing follow-on funds.
hints: Wrong: pre-commitment activity.
Wrong: pre-commitment activity.
Wrong: pre-commitment activity.
Correct: drawdown liaison happens after commitment.
